chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shaban is my month and Ramadan is the month of Allah, and it is the spring of the poor. And the sacrifice (Al-Adha) was made only so that your poor may eat meat to satiety, so feed them.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The ritual sacrifice of an animal, typically associated with Eid al-Adha
key_terms.رَبِيعُ الْفُقَرَاءِ: Spring of the poor, a metaphor for renewal and abundance for the needy
key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the month of Shaban and its connection to charity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) distinguishes Shaban as his personal month and Ramadan as Allah's, while characterizing Shaban as the 'spring of the poor' to emphasize its role in nurturing spiritual and material sustenance. He connects the ritual of sacrifice (Udhiyah) directly to the welfare of the needy, instructing believers to provide meat for satiety, thereby linking ritual worship with social justice. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between devotional acts and charitable obligations, where Shaban serves as a preparatory period for the generosity of Ramadan.
